Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
820 PM EDT Sat Sep 19 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Added some light sprinkles in across western and central MD this 
evening. Additional scattered showers early Sunday morning and again 
Sunday afternoon as a front slides through. Small Craft
Advisories expanded.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Scattered showers and perhaps a few thunderstorms look to 
finish out the weekend as a front passes through. 

- 2) Daily shower chances and cooler temperatures persists through 
midweek with drier conditions for the upcoming weekend. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Scattered showers and perhaps a few thunderstorms look to 
finish out the weekend as a front passes through. 

Added some light showers and sprinkles in across central and western 
MD this evening as spotty activity drops south from central and 
western PA. Outside of these showers and sprinkles, is increased low 
and mid level cloudiness. This is in association with a squeeze play 
between fronts with moisture advection increasing from the south and 
east and a cold front slowly dropping down from the Great Lakes 
region. Low and mid level clouds will remain abundant overnight with 
some filtered breaks the further south you get toward the I-64 
corridor. Most will remain dry overnight, but with moisture 
advection increasing over a shallow cool layer aloft expect humidity 
values to gradually climb and spotty showers likely developing over 
the mountains heading into Sunday morning. This shower activity will 
be scattered in nature and in association with the warm front and 
lead piece of shortwave energy ahead of the front that is currently 
located back across the eastern Great Lakes and Ohio River Valley. 
The first round of showers should exit the area around midday with a 
secondary area of showers and perhaps a few thunderstorms working 
through the region Sunday afternoon and evening as the cold front 
drops through. Current hi-res guidance has slowed the front up a bit 
while dissipating/washing it out over the region Sunday evening into 
Sunday night. Deterministic synoptic guidance has a similar 
solution while keeping a ripple of low pressure riding along the
boundary Sunday evening into Sunday night forcing it south. 
With that said, severe weather does not appear to be a concern 
although a few thunderstorm cannot be ruled out over central VA,
southern MD, and the northern neck of VA where some breaks of 
sun may filter through. Any of these storms will be capable of 
locally gusty winds, heavy rainfall, and lightning. 

The front will eventually shunt southward heading into Monday 
morning although on and off shower activity will persists into 
the new workweek given increased onshore flow. Expect a 
noticeable cooling trend beginning Monday in the wake of the 
cold front late Sunday night. Highs Sunday will push into the 
upper 70s and low 80s (low 70s mountains) with overnight lows in
the upper 50s and mid 60s. Highs Monday will struggle to get 
out of the upper 60s and low 70s as more of a wedging pattern 
sets up with increasing onshore flow. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Daily shower chances and cooler temperatures persists through 
midweek with drier conditions for the upcoming weekend. 

Mid-level moisture overhead will coincide with an area of low 
pressure just off the East Coast tracking north on Wednesday. Weak 
instability at the surface will suppress thunderstorm activity for 
the most part, but expect rain showers to continue through Wednesday 
and Thursday as shortwave disturbances track across the Mid- 
Atlantic. High temperatures continue to range in the 60s as 
these disturbances move through. 

As the coastal low skirts the Mid-Atlantic coastline, winds will 
be elevated Wednesday and Thursday with wind gusts between 20-30 MPH 
possible, especially along the Chesapeake Bay. Winds could 
potentially be higher over the waters, and this onshore flow 
combined with stronger tidal influence could increase coastal flood 
risk during this period. Refer to the coastal flooding section below 
for more details. 

As this system tracks north towards the end of the week, winds along 
the coastline should gradually decrease. Mid-level dry air moves in 
overhead from the Midwest, which should lead to diminishing rainfall 
potential heading into the weekend.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
VFR conditions look to continue through at least 02z/10pm with 
MVFR cigs settling in overnight as low and mid level clouds 
thicken. Low and mid level clouds will persists through Sunday 
afternoon as a result of increased moisture advection ahead of a
series of fronts pushing through. Most locations will remain 
dry tonight outside of a passing shower or sprinkle for 
terminals west of MRB. Shower coverage will increase early to 
mid Sunday morning between 10- 16z/6am-12pm as a result of a 
warm front lifting into the region. Moisture advection with this
front combined with a leading piece of shortwave energy will 
yield scattered light to moderate showers mainly at terminals 
north of KCHO. Expect a lull in the showers midday with an 
additional round of scattered showers and perhaps a few 
thunderstorms Sunday afternoon beyond 19z-23z/3-7pm. Greatest 
opportunity for a thunderstorm would be south of the corridor 
from DCA down to CHO/RIC where breaks of sun will be more 
prevalent. Severe weather is not expected although locally gusty
winds and brief heavy rain cannot be ruled out with any 
thunderstorms that form. CIGS become more scattered to broken 
Sunday evening into Sunday night before restrictions return 
Monday as onshore east to northeast flow increases. 

Expect a mashup of MVFR to perhaps periods of IFR cigs on both 
Monday and Tuesday as a result of increased onshore flow. Low and 
mid level cloudiness will be persistent through midweek along with 
daily chances for showers. Sub-VFR conditions could persist through 
Thursday as scattered showers continue throughout the region. Gusty 
winds between 20-25 knots are possible on Thursday. Winds flow from 
northeasterly to northerly by Friday. 

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisories have been expanded to encompass not only the 
open waters of the bay and tidal Potomac, but the middle waters of 
bay north toward the Baltimore Inner Harbor. SCA level winds will 
continue on and off through Sunday midday as onshore flow increases 
and the gradient tightens ahead of the incumbent frontal boundaries. 
Additional SCA level conditions may be needed for the waters late 
Sunday afternoon and evening and again early next week. 

North to northeasterly wind gusts remain elevated through Wednesday 
and Thursday as an area of low pressure remains off the East Coast. 
Showers & a couple of thunderstorms are possible over the waters 
during this period. As this system begins to track north late in the 
week, winds should begin to decrease heading into the weekend. 

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Coastal Flood Advisory has been issued for Anne Arundel County.
CBOFS guidance seems like the only guidance performing well with
the elevated water levels and showing the rapid response due to
the onshore flow. 

Onshore flow will persist through at least the middle of next
week with water levels remaining elevated with minor coastal
flooding expected at times of high tide. At this time, the risk
of moderate coastal flooding seems low.

&&
